title: Burpee's loss
basis: The ORB editor's note; the two differ by seven minutes.

records.says: Shot down at 0200 immediately south of Gilze-Rijen (Netherlands) on way to target.
records.label: ORB editor's note

title: Ottley's loss
basis: Brown's sighting, the one direct observation.

records.says: At 0231, Group sent the code word “Gilbert” to AJ-C, and the signal was acknowledged.
The second signal was not acknowledged, indicating that AJ-C had met its fate at about 0231.
Ken Brown, flying AJ-F a few minutes behind, reported seeing him hit the ground at 0235.
Maudslay is shot down by flak at Klein-Netterden, near Emmerich, at 0236; all are killed.

title: Young's loss
basis: The ORB editor's note; the two differ by a minute.

records.says: "Dinghy" Young's Lancaster was shot down by flak North of Ijmuiden at 0258 (Castricum aan Zee) killing all the crew.
records.label: ORB editor's note

records.says: Anderson, his rear turret unserviceable and the valleys filling with mist, turns back with his mine at 0310.
Brown attacks the Sorpe from 60 ft at 0314 after marking it with incendiaries; the crest holds.
Townsend drops on his third run at 0337; the mine bounces twice and explodes short.

title: Townsend's target
basis: Townsend's own report; the dams' coordinates put the Bever 11 km south of the Ennepe, not north-west.

records.says: Post war research proves that Townsend attacked not the Ennerpe Dam but the Bever Dam nearby to the North West instead.
records.label: ORB editor's note

records.says: Sweetman (2002) makes a strong case that the fourth dam attacked was the Bever Dam

title: The Eder flood down the valley
basis: Wabern's arrival is the one time found below the dam; the front runs there from the breach at an even pace through Affoldern, Bergheim, Wega and Fritzlar.

records.says: In der Folge ergoss sich eine 6 bis 8 m hohe Flutwelle durch das untere Edertal nach Fritzlar, Wabern und Felsberg
Um 5.30 Uhr traf die Flutwelle ein
